objective:
Build Burrowkeep, a one-page mining-and-raising game beside Squeekchain. The real hamster's settled wheel counts become ore for the player's mill. Ore is spent on food, raising the mill hamster, or tightening the player's gears. Upgrades never make the real hamster run faster and never feed him. Say that in the page. No wallet, no betting, no dashboard of block height or supply.

Ore is booked only from single-round system.settlement_completed events on GET https://api.squeekchain.com/v1/events?category=protocol&limit=100, schemaVersion 3, chainId 11155111, confirmationStatus safe. Work is the decimal string workAdded, parsed as an integer. At hamster level 1, every 20 counts is 1 ore. Each hamster level lowers that by 3, to a minimum of 8. Gear level adds (level-1) extra ore on a round with work greater than 0. If food is 0 when the round is booked, keep only half the ore, rounded down. A round with 0 work books nothing and does not spend food. A running round spends 1 food after the ore is booked. Food, hamster, and gears each cap at 5. Food costs 5 ore. Hamster upgrades cost 10, 20, 40, 80. Gear upgrades cost 8, 16, 32, 64. A hand crank gives 1 ore and then waits 8 seconds. Only rounds after the player opens the mill are booked. The open round may show an unbooked estimate from live cumulative work, clearly labeled as not booked. The painted burrow shows a wheel that eases to the live RPM and a gear that turns with the player's gear level. Default language Chinese, with an English toggle. Footer in English: Burrowkeep is a mill beside the real wheel. Upgrades do not make Squeektoshi run. Testnet only.
